subject.title: Bug: Telegram delivery queue recovery can replay old sendMessage replies and duplicate delivery-mirror transcript entries

question: How should OpenClaw treat legacy pending Telegram delivery-queue rows that lack recoveryState/idempotency metadata after migration?
rationale: Source inspection proves old rows can bypass the current recovery guard, but the correct behavior trades off duplicate visible sends against dropping or indefinitely delaying a delivery that may not have landed.

options.title: Quarantine or migrate ambiguous legacy rows
options.body: Move legacy Telegram rows without recoveryState to failed/quarantine, or mark them unknown_after_send without replay, and add migration plus recovery coverage before closing the issue.

options.title: Preserve pending until reconciliation exists
options.body: Mark legacy rows unknown and leave them pending/backed off until Telegram gains a reconcileUnknownSend path or an operator surface can decide.

options.title: Accept legacy replay risk
options.body: Leave old unmarked rows replayable and accept that upgrades from affected releases may duplicate visible Telegram replies and transcript mirrors.

recommendation.title: Quarantine or migrate ambiguous legacy rows
recommendation.body: Move legacy Telegram rows without recoveryState to failed/quarantine, or mark them unknown_after_send without replay, and add migration plus recovery coverage before closing the issue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across outbound recovery, storage, migrations, and related delivery-state tradeoffs.
